title: Tennessee Multi-Sector Plan for Aging Data Dashboard V2
description: The Tennessee Multi-Sector Plan for Aging Data Dashboard Version 2 offers the most recent, comprehensive, and actionable data to support policymakers and community partners in enhancing the well-being of Tennessee residents aged 65 and older. This dashboard provides extensive data and statistics on various aspects of aging, including demographics, health and well-being, economic security, social engagement, community support, and more.

The dashboard features an advanced, user-friendly interface that enables policymakers and community members to access and analyze data visually and interactively, facilitating targeted interventions and informed policy development. The expansion incorporates a broader range of data, integrates qualitative insights, and enhances user interaction to address the multifaceted aspects of aging, such as improving awareness, prevention, early detection, and care management of chronic conditions like Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
This dashboard is a joint effort of the Tennessee Department of Health Office of Healthy Aging and the East Tennessee State University Center for Rural Health and Research.

Ambulatory Surgical Treatment Centers are facilities where surgeries that do not require hospital admission are performed

Assisted Care Living Facilities are residential facilities for individuals who need some assistance with daily activities such as bathing, dressing, or medication management, but do not require full-time medical care like in a nursing home
Birthing Centers are health care facilities specializing in childbirth, designed to provide a homelike environment
Home Health Agencies are organizations that provide health care services to patients in their own homes
Hospice facilities offer palliative and end-of-life care to patients with terminal illnesses
Hospitals are institutions that provide a wide range of medical, surgical, and emergency services
Nursing Homes are long-term care facilities offering 24/7 medical supervision and assistance with daily activities for individuals with chronic illnesses, disabilities, or cognitive impairments
Outpatient Diagnostic Centers are facilities that perform diagnostic tests (e.g., X-rays, MRIs, blood tests) without requiring hospital admission

Geriatricians are physicians specialized in caring for adults aged 65 and older, play a critical role in managing age-related conditions such as chronic illnesses, cognitive decline, mobility limitations, and medication complexity
